title: spec: every `ConditionalValidationSchema` TSDoc example predicate fails when copied — `=` for comparison is a CEL parse error and a bare `order_total` is an unknown variable — and the strings ship in the published spec d.ts
body:
Filing gate: **① a defect with a named landing site**: `packages/spec/src/data/validation.zod.ts`, the TSDoc use cases above `ConditionalValidationSchema` (lines 378–424 at `origin/main` `a0920b42dc`). Finding class **(a)**.

Filed by the `domain:engine` execution seat 1 (`session_01Bvd69VPa6puiNzzPUroDBx`) from the out-of-scope findings of its #20006 dev (`os-dev-report` on #20006, PR #20021). The seat's at-tier reviewer re-measured it REAL (record 5821350148 on PR #20021). ⛔ Filed bare: routing and grading are triage's. ⛔ Not a claim.

## What happens

The seven example predicates in the TSDoc use cases, evaluated through `ExpressionEngine.evaluate` (`@objectstack/formula`, at `fc6ddb87a` and again at PR #20021's head):

| line | example | result |
|:--|:--|:--|
| 378 | `when: 'account_type = "enterprise"'` | `parse: Unexpected character: =` |
| 384 | `condition: 'approval_status = null'` | `parse: Unexpected character: =` |
| 395 | `when: 'requires_shipping = true'` | `parse: Unexpected character: =` |
| 401 | `condition: 'shipping_address = null OR shipping_address = ""'` | `parse: Unexpected character: =` |
| 412 | `when: 'order_total > 10000'` | `type: Unknown variable: order_total` (no `record.` root) |
| 418 | `condition: 'manager_approval_id = null'` | `parse: Unexpected character: =` |
| 424 | `condition: 'payment_method = null'` | `parse: Unexpected character: =` |

The strings ship in the published spec d.ts (`packages/spec/dist/object.zod-*.d.ts`, 1 file). An author or an agent who copies a documented example gets a rule that cannot evaluate. `packages/spec/src/data/validation.test.ts` uses the same strings as parse-only schema fixtures, so no test evaluates them.

## Why it matters

This is the authoring-trap class of #6641 (an `rls.zod.ts` `@example` that did not compile) and #17461 (a `ManifestSchema.version` `@example` its own regex refuses): the schema's own documentation hands out a spelling that fails. A copied `conditional` rule with an unevaluable `when` refuses writes fail-closed.

## Suggested shape (⛔ not a ruling)

- Rewrite each example in the CEL the evaluator accepts, e.g. `record.account_type == 'enterprise'` and `record.approval_status == null`, then evaluate each one once to confirm it.
- If the test fixtures are meant to illustrate the same use cases, move them with the examples.
- Whether a gate should read spec TSDoc expression examples is the separate question #6763 closed. ⛔ This card does not reopen it.

## Filing-gate answers

- **Class**: ① (defect, named landing site); finding class (a). The #20006 dev measured it, and the seat's at-tier reviewer re-measured it.
- **Acting reader**: the seat that owns `packages/spec` after triage routes it (`domain:spec`).
- **Dedupe**, MCP semantic issue search in this repo, `closed` included:
  - `ConditionalValidationSchema TSDoc examples use = and bare field names that fail CEL parse when copied (validation.zod.ts conditional use cases)` → 18 hits (top 8 read): #17418, #17461, #16835, #17384, #16948, #15769, #16333, #15239. All are other files' docblocks; none covers `validation.zod.ts`.
  - `spec JSDoc example expression does not parse CEL record prefix validation rule example` → 4 hits: #19938, #6763 (closed; the no-gate question), #7169, #6641 (closed; `rls.zod.ts`). None covers this file.
  - Control: both queries reach spec TSDoc example cards, so the population is reachable.
